provenance: Invented cross-domain teaching controls; not private manuscript text or verified research results.
evaluation_boundary: Fixture and package checks do not establish semantic correctness, real reading, human comprehension or measured improvement.

facts: Staff quality-control daily readings to produce a corrected series.
Forecasts consume that corrected series, not the raw readings.
A terminology scan found no configured phrase conflicts.
cases.text:
Staff prepare the daily readings. The forecast model uses the corrected series.

The quality-control step produces the corrected series.
criteria: Put production of the corrected series before its forecast use and preserve its identity.
Explain the actual dependency; a clean scan or added connector alone is not acceptance.

facts: The uncertainty summary and spatial plot are independent products of the same dataset.
No execution order or concurrent implementation is documented.
cases.text: We calculate the uncertainty summary. Then we produce the spatial plot.
criteria: Identify unsupported sequential implication without asserting that independent products are computed simultaneously.
Do not invent an implementation order; distinguish optional phrasing from verified execution.

facts: Before each simulation run, users select the input variables once.
During the run, a data service updates their values daily.
Users do not manually reselect variables each day.
cases.text: Each morning, users define the model inputs. The simulation then uses those inputs.
criteria: Separate once-per-run variable selection from daily updates by the data service.
Preserve actor and frequency; do not invent additional daily manual tasks.

facts: The forecast is calculated before comparison with observations.
The later diagnostic records forecast error.
Diagnostic findings neither stop nor modify the forecast.
cases.text: The forecast is compared with observations. If the diagnostic fails, the forecast stops.
criteria: Remove the invented stop/veto and retain report-only diagnostic behavior.
Keep forecast generation distinct from the later observation comparison.

facts: Every survey interview uses a core questionnaire.
An optional interview module can supply contextual examples.
The optional module is not required to analyze core questionnaire responses.
cases.text: We administer the core questionnaire. Once the contextual interview module is complete, we analyze the responses.
criteria: Do not make the optional module a prerequisite for core analysis.
Retain the module's contextual function without forcing an experimental workflow onto survey description.

facts: Only the paragraph is supplied; no implementation or protocol can be consulted.
The actor, update frequency and effect of the check are unspecified.
cases.text: The inputs are prepared. The process checks them and continues.
criteria: State which workflow facts are unavailable and what would establish them.
Do not fill the gap with daily automation, a human operator, validation success, or a stop policy.

facts: The author has locked the wording and requested diagnosis only.
A supplied protocol says recorded values are screened before the analyst estimates the model.
cases.text: The analyst estimates the model from recorded values. The values are screened after estimation.
criteria: Locate the conflict and describe a conditional/minimal repair without rewriting the author-locked text.
Do not claim an applied correction or fully accepted passage.

facts: Users choose variables once before a run.
A service refreshes their values daily; complete values feed the forecast.
Missing required values stop that day's calculation.
cases.text: Users choose the variables before a run. A service refreshes their values daily. The forecast uses these updated values; if a required value is missing, that day's calculation stops.
criteria: Retain this clear sequence and branch; no additional transition or restated definition is required.
Do not add unreported mechanics or create a review ledger.

facts: The author's local comment asks to clarify that raw measurements go into quality control.
Quality control outputs corrected measurements, which then feed the model.
The following sentence refers to 'these measurements'.
cases.text: The measurements enter the model's quality-control step. These measurements drive the forecast.
criteria: Address the raw-input comment and inspect the neighbor so the forecast unambiguously uses corrected measurements.
Do not preserve an ambiguous 'these' simply because the annotated phrase was repaired.

facts: Correct agreement only in the first sentence.
The second sentence and all technical meaning are locked.
cases.text: The samples was stored at 4°C. The assay measured enzyme activity.
criteria: Change only 'was' to 'were', preserving the temperature, assay sentence and meaning.
Do not audit the full section, demand workflow evidence, or create project files.

facts: This conceptual paragraph contrasts two ethical positions, not procedural stages.
No temporal or causal sequence is asserted.
cases.text: One position evaluates decisions by their consequences. The other evaluates whether decisions satisfy duties. The contrast concerns the basis for evaluation, not the order in which decisions occur.
criteria: Retain the explicit conceptual contrast without imposing input/action/output stages.
Do not demand a study area, experimental results or pipeline bridge.

facts: For each batch, complete files are required before scoring.
Incomplete batches stop before scoring.
Only batches with reference labels receive an optional later diagnostic; it reports differences without altering scores.
cases.text: Each batch is checked for required files. If a file is missing, processing stops before scoring; otherwise, the complete batch is scored. For batches with reference labels, an optional later diagnostic reports differences without altering the scores.
criteria: Retain the clear prerequisite, stop branch and optional report-only diagnostic.
Do not remove helpful conditional connectors or invent parallel execution.
